Other words

  • aegrōtus, aegrōta, aegrōtum — ill, sick

    also used · classical · Traupman 65; Traupman 55: Esne tū aegrōta?, are you sick?; Traupman 331 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • aegrōtō, aegrōtāre — be ill

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 331 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • in morbum incidere — fall ill

    also used · classical · Traupman 65; Traupman 313; Traupman 331

  • morbō corripī — come down with an illness

    also used · modern · Traupman 95; Traupman 294

  • valētūdinārius, valētūdināria, valētūdinārium — sickly, an invalid

    also used · classical · Varr. RR 2.1.15 (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ira 3.33.2 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 62, for “bedridden” · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: not in Cicero; one in poor health generally, not only one kept in bed.

  • male validus — sickly, not strong

    also used · classical · Traupman 65

See also I don’t feel well, fever, disease, suffer.
